description: Interactive step-based geometry constructor for Grade 7 Mathematics — Linear Pair Angle Finder. Redesigned with the Singularity Design System: Poppins font, purple (#4A4DC9) / orange (#FF7212) palette, pill-shaped buttons (border-radius 40, height 40px), gradient header (purple-dark → purple → orange-mid). Learn mode progressively reveals four angles using linear pair property. Practice mode has 5 MCQ questions with correct/wrong feedback, explanations, score tracking, and results screen. SVG diagram updates per question. Touch-friendly for tablet use. Indian school context.
curriculum: NCERT Ganita Prakash Grade 7, Chapter 5 — Parallel and Intersecting Lines
learningObjectives: Understand that two intersecting lines form four angles
Learn the linear pair property: adjacent angles on a straight line add up to 180°
Discover that vertically opposite angles are always equal
Apply the linear pair property to find unknown angles step by step
Test understanding through MCQ practice with immediate feedback

learn.description: Step-by-step guided exploration. Step 1: show ∠a. Step 2: linear pair (a,b) → find ∠b. Step 3: linear pair (b,c) → find ∠c. Step 4: linear pair (c,d) → find ∠d. Step 5: vertically opposite pairs with purple/orange highlights.

practice.description: 5 MCQ questions with pill-shaped option buttons. Correct → green bg (#E8F8F0) + pop animation. Wrong → red bg (#FDECEB) + shake + correct highlighted in green. Explanation in orange-light (#FFF3E4) box. Progress bar with purple→orange gradient. Final results with score badge, emoji, per-question dots, and gradient retake button.

practiceFeatures.feedbackOnWrongAnswer: Selected option shakes red (#FDECEB bg, #E74C3C border). Correct option pops green (#E8F8F0 bg, #2ECC71 border). Explanation in orange-light (#FFF3E4) box with #FC9145 left border.
practiceFeatures.feedbackOnCorrectAnswer: Green pop animation with #E8F8F0 background and '✓ Correct! Well done!' message.
practiceFeatures.scoreTracking: Progress bar with purple→orange gradient. Star icon + score counter. Final screen: emoji, gradient score badge (borderRadius: 40), per-question check/cross dots, gradient 'Retake Quiz' button.
practiceFeatures.diagramUpdate: SVG updates per question. Before answer: only given angle shown. After answer: all relevant angles revealed with linear pair / vertically opposite highlights.

instructions_for_student: In Learn mode, use the pill-shaped navigation buttons to step through. Watch as each angle is revealed — notice which two angles form a linear pair (add to 180°). After all four are found, observe vertically opposite angles are equal. In Practice mode, answer 5 multiple-choice questions. If you choose a wrong answer, the correct answer will be highlighted in green with an explanation.

teaching_notes.step_1: Show only angle a = 120° (purple arc) and the two intersecting lines. Ask the student what they think the other angles might be.
teaching_notes.step_2: Highlight the linear pair (a, b) with a dashed purple-light arc. Calculate b = 180 − 120 = 60. ∠b shown in orange-mid.
teaching_notes.step_3: Highlight the linear pair (b, c). Calculate c = 180 − 60 = 120. ∠c shown in purple-dark. Ask the student to predict before revealing.
teaching_notes.step_4: Highlight (c, d). Calculate d = 180 − 120 = 60. ∠d shown in orange.
teaching_notes.step_5: Highlight vertically opposite pairs: ∠a = ∠c in purple bg (#EEEDF7), ∠b = ∠d in orange bg (#FFF3E4). Equality symbols animated.
teaching_notes.practice: 5 MCQ questions of increasing difficulty. Q1-Q2 test linear pairs. Q3 tests vertically opposite. Q4 combines both. Q5 requires multi-step reasoning (sum of two angles).
